description: White releases the central tension on move 3 for a symmetrical, open position — the antithesis of the locked Advance and the complex Winawer. Both sides develop naturally and the game turns on piece activity and small positional edges rather than pawn-chain warfare.

lines.description: After 1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5, White dissolves the tension at once with 3.exd5 exd5. Both sides develop simply: 4.Nf3 Nf6 5.Bd3 Bd6. With the center wide open, piece activity is everything — White aims for quick development and the e5 outpost, Black for ...O-O, ...Bg4, and pressure on d4. A clean positional struggle that teaches development habits.
